title: Investigating the Effectiveness of Calisda, a Digital Health Intervention for Patients With Menopause Symptoms
official: Investigating the Effectiveness of Calisda, a Digital Health Intervention for Patients With Menopause Symptoms: Randomized Controlled Trial (CHIME Trial)
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out if calisda, a digital health intervention, can help women with menopause symptoms manage their symptoms and improve their quality of life.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does calisda, together with regular treatment, improve health outcomes after six months better than regular treatment alone?
* Are the positive effects of calisda already noticeable after three months?

Researchers will compare two groups:

* Intervention group: Participants use the calisda intervention and continue their usual treatment.
* Control group: Participants continue with their usual treatment only.

Participants will:

* Fill out questionnaires online at the start of the study, after 3 months, and after 6 months
* Continue with their usual treatment (both groups) and use calisda, a digital health intervention, for six months (intervention group only)
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Female biological sex
* Age 40-65 years
* Diagnosis of menopause symptoms (ICD-10 code: N95.1) confirmed by a medical document
* Increased levels of menopause symptoms (MRS-II total score ≥ 14)
* Reduced menopause-specific quality of life (MENQOL total score ≥ 3)
* Stable symptom-related treatment (medication, psychotherapy, no treatment, …) for at least 60 days at the time of inclusion
* Sufficient knowledge of the German language
* Basic computer skills required for independent use of a digital intervention
* Consent to participation

Exclusion Criteria:

* Plans to change symptom-related treatment (medication, psychotherapy, …) in the upcoming 6 months after inclusion
* Current or history of any malignancy except for basal and squamous cell skin tumors
* Current HRT use
* Premature, medically induced menopause (e.g. following bilateral oophorectomy)
* Known somatic or psychiatric condition that might interfere with successful study participation (e.g. unstable neurologic or psychiatric disorder)
* Previous use of a digital intervention for menopause symptoms (including calisda) or another digital intervention developed by GAIA.
